Hi all,

We have advanced with Petr Novak (SWE II candidate, currently in Prague). He completed interviews last week and his expectation is ~€90k gross (local currency). Based on our US-equivalent banding, this maps to a mid-high SWE II offer if we convert using local market rates + a COLA uplift.

Attached is the draft offer (PDF) and a quick Prague COLA workbook I pulled together (prague-cola-index-2026.xlsx). Proposed comp in local terms: base €88,000 + standard Redwood benefits. Equivalent USD reference is ~ $95k — but that understates Prague market movement. My ask: approval for a one-time geo uplift of +6% over the SWE II midpoint for Prague hires to remain competitive, and explicit sign-off to extend an offer at €88k (or adjust to rounding per finance).

Why: multiple offers in the last two months for Prague-based candidates have priced ~4–8% above our previous benchmark. Candidate is strong, interview feedback green across the board, ready to take offer this week.

Request: please confirm (1) compensation approval, (2) whether we should include a Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA) clause for annual review, and (3) any changes to the banding guidance before I send.

Thanks,
Neha

Hannah, team —

Thanks for the packet. Quick summary from market comps in Prague (engineering ICs, mid-senior): median base is ~€76–84k for what you call SWE II; 90th percentile pushes into low €90s. My recommendation: approve a one-time geographic uplift of 6% for Prague for hires in the next 6 months (market is rising fast) and formalize a quarterly review of the COLA table.

Offer language (suggested):
"Base salary is set in local currency. Redwood periodically reviews location-based cost of living and market differentials and may adjust base salary accordingly. Any such adjustments are at company discretion and subject to local laws."

Sign-on guidance: small, single-payment sign-ons are standard (1–3 months base pro-rata) for counter offers in Prague; only grant if candidate has a verifiable counter.

I'll also note: if Redwood wants a repeatable policy, consider a band overlay (e.g., add a +5–7% multiplier to EU Eastern hubs). It reduces negotiation cycles and keeps offers consistent.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call if you want to run comps live.

Regards,
Sarah Green
